notes: Wiring follows the circuit image and the pin table: ST->A0, Z->A1, Y->A2, X->A3, GND->A4, VDD->A5. A4 is driven LOW as ground and A5 HIGH as 5V in code. The schematic crosses X/Z, but the image and table are taken as authoritative.

The breakout's 6-pin header sits in breadboard columns 4-9 at the row nearest the top of the image (labelled j in the image). The catalogue's top bank 't' is rows a-e, so I used 't' holes: module in row e, wires in row d of the same columns. Any hole in the same column-bank is the same strip, so the connectivity is unchanged.
The Arduino is assumed to be powered over USB, which the manual does not show, so no USB cable is included.
The ADXL335 catalogue type stands in for the generic ADXL3xx breakout. Its ports are ST, Z, Y, X, GND, VCC, and VDD on the board is mapped to VCC.
The MCP connectors (Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive) need authorization, but they were not used for this task.

The tutorial gives two alternative circuits (potentiometer OR photoresistor + 10k resistor). Both use A0, so only the potentiometer circuit is built here. The photoresistor variant would replace pot1 with a photoresistor from 5V to A0 plus a 10k resistor from A0 to GND.

In the potentiometer image the yellow wire ends in the top half of the breadboard just above the pot. I assumed it is meant to reach the pot's middle pin, as the text says, so I put it in the same strip as the middle leg (11b.d).
Pot outer pins: GND to the black wire and VCC (5V) to the red wire, as in the image. The two outer pins are interchangeable.

The optional external LED circuit (pin 13 -> 220 ohm resistor -> LED anode, cathode -> GND) is not in the images. Its breadboard positions (columns 20-25, top half) are my choice. The built-in LED on pin 13 also works.
Which GND.n is which on the Uno is assumed: GND.1 is on the power header, GND.3 is the GND pin next to pin 13.
Breadboard hole positions are estimated from the image.
The text says one outer pin goes to GND and the other outer pin to 5V. The image shows black (GND) on the left outer pin and red (5V) on the right outer pin, so I used that.
Exact breadboard columns and rows are estimated from the image. I put the pot legs in 10b.f, 11b.f and 12b.f, and the wires in row g of the same columns.
The yellow wire appears to end at the pot body in the image. I assumed it plugs into the same column strip as the middle (wiper) pin.
The pot is wired GND (outer), SIG (middle), VCC (outer), as in the schematic.
The USB cable to the computer is not shown in the circuit, so I left it out.
The black wire goes to the GND pin in the power header (GND.1). The red wire goes to 5V and the yellow wire to A0.
In the image the breadboard is drawn with rows j..f on top and a..e on the bottom, so the top half maps to catalogue bank 'b' (rows f-j) and the bottom half to bank 't' (rows a-e).

Fixed the single-use hole conflicts: each wire and the pot leg that share a column now use different holes of the same 5-hole strip. The pot legs are in row e (22t.e GND, 24t.e VCC) and row f (23b.f wiper). The black GND wire is in 22t.d, the red 5V wire in 24t.d and the yellow wire in 23b.g. The wire and leg in each pair are electrically the same node.
Column numbers were estimated from the image: resistor 4g-6g, LED anode 6h / cathode 8h, black LED-ground wire at 8g, blue pin-9 wire at 4f.
The pot straddles the centre gap: its wiper pin is in the top half (column 23) and the two outer legs are in the bottom half (columns 22 and 24).
The LED's longer anode leg goes to the resistor's strip. The cathode goes to ground through the black wire, as the text says.
Uno GND pin choice: the power-header GND is GND.1 and the digital-header GND next to pin 13 is GND.3. Both are the same ground net.
Resistor value is 220 ohm per the manual. The schematic shows the pot's outer pins on 5V and GND and the wiper on A0.

Each of the 12 channels is a jumper wire from Mega pins 13 down to 2 into the breadboard bottom half (bank 't'), a 220 ohm resistor across the centre gap, a red LED in the upper half (bank 'b'), and a black jumper from the LED cathode column to the ground rail. The ground rail is wired to a Mega GND pin.

Pin-to-column mapping read from the circuit image: 13->col2, 12->4, 11->6, 10->8, 9->10, 8->12, 7->15, 6->17, 5->20, 4->23, 3->26, 2->28. The LED anode shares the resistor's column, and the cathode is in the next column (N+1).

The image shows the breadboard rotated, so rows a-e are at the bottom and f-j at the top. I mapped the bottom half to bank 't' and the top half to bank 'b'. Exact row letters (c, e, f, h, j) are approximate.
The catalogue doesn't say which rail is the top ground rail. I used 'tn' and numbered its holes to match the column position of each wire. Rail hole numbers are approximate.

The manual calls for 220 ohm resistors, red LEDs and 'hook-up wires', and I used jumper-wire for all of them. The tutorial doesn't use the Mega GND header pin number, so I used GND.1 for the ground wire. The image shows it going to the digital-side GND next to AREF.

The manual's main wiring photo shows two UNO boards with 'old style' wiring (D10->RESET, D11->D11, D12->D12, D13->D13, 5V, GND). I used that: uno1 is the programmer and uno2 is the target. The ICSP-header wiring and the Nano/MEGA/MKR1000 variants are alternatives and aren't modelled.

The 10uF capacitor goes between the programmer's RESET and GND, with the positive leg on RESET. The manual says to fit it after the ArduinoISP sketch is uploaded. It is shown on the breadboard, with the programmer RESET and GND brought in by jumper wires.

The three optional LEDs from the ArduinoISP sketch are included. Heartbeat is on D9, error on D8 and programming on D7, which are the sketch's default pins. The manual doesn't give resistor values, so I assumed 220 ohm for each LED. Breadboard hole positions are assumed.

The manual says not to power the boards while wiring. The USB cable is shown on the programmer only, since it is needed to upload the sketch and run the programming. The target is powered from the programmer's 5V.

The Arduino IDE settings are software only and not part of the graph: Board 'Arduino Nano' / Processor ATmega328P in the screenshot (the target board type), Programmer 'Arduino as ISP', then Burn Bootloader. The memory-map figure is also not part of the graph.
The usb-cable catalogue entry has no ports, so its joined edge to uno1 has no port names.
The sketch uses the built-in LED on D13, so the external LED circuit is optional. I built it because the task asks for it.
The breadboard image labels its top half rows j-f. The catalogue calls rows f-j bank 'b', so I used 'b' for the top half as drawn.

Orange wire: Uno pin 13 to column 3, row g. Resistor: column 3 row h to column 6 row h. LED anode (bent, long leg): column 6 row i. LED cathode: column 8 row i. Black wire: column 8 row g to the GND pin beside pin 13 (GND.1).
The schematic shows the GND connection at the bottom GND pin. The photo wires the black lead to the GND header next to pin 13. I followed the photo, since both are the same GND net.
The USB cable to the computer is mentioned only for uploading the sketch, so I did not add it.

The graph models the first diagram (burning the bootloader with the Arduino as ISP) in the full external-clock configuration. The second diagram (USB-serial upload, microcontroller removed from the Arduino, RX/TX wired to the ATmega) and the minimal no-crystal circuit are not included as separate graphs.
The diagram labels the chip ATmega168; the text says ATmega328P, so the catalogue type atmega328p is used. Both are 28-pin DIPs with the same pinout.

The chip is placed with pin 1 at the bottom-left, notch to the left. Pins 1-14 are in the bottom half (row f) at columns 3-16. Pins 15-28 are in the top half (row e) at columns 16 down to 3. The exact columns are estimated from the image.

ISP wiring: Arduino 10 to RESET (pin 1), 11 to MOSI (pin 17), 12 to MISO (pin 18), 13 to SCK (pin 19). 5V and GND go to the breadboard rails. The rails supply VCC (pin 7), AVCC (pin 20), and GND (pins 8 and 22).
The 10k resistor goes from the reset strip to the 5V rail, as a reset pull-up. The picture shows the resistor leg going to the bottom rail.
The crystal sits across XTAL pins 9 and 10 through two blue jumper wires, as in the diagram. Each 22 pF capacitor goes from a crystal leg to the ground rail.
Rail hole numbers (tp.N, tn.N, bp.N, bn.N) are approximate. Long red and black wires on the right of the breadboard join the top and bottom rails, as in the picture.
Pin 21 (AREF) is left unconnected.

Breadboard orientation: the image's upper main section (labelled f-j) is treated as bank 'b'. Exact columns are read from the image: resistor in 3b.h and 6b.h, LED anode (bent, long leg) in 6b.i, cathode in 8b.i.
Orange wire links Uno pin 13 to column 3 (3b.g); black wire links Uno GND (the GND pin next to AREF, taken as GND.1) to column 8 (8b.g).
Circuit path: pin 13 -> resistor -> LED anode; LED cathode -> GND.
The manual says to use a 220 ohm resistor; the sketch itself (BlinkWithoutDelay) is not part of the graph.
The Uno's built-in pin 13 LED is not modelled.

Breadboard hole names follow the image row letters: the upper half (rows f-j in the picture) is written as bank 'b' and the lower half (rows a-e) as bank 't'. This differs from the catalogue's description, so the bank letters may need swapping.

Each LED sits in the upper half with anode in column 7/10/13/16/19/22 and cathode in the next column. The schematic shows pin -> 220 ohm resistor -> LED anode -> ground, so the leg in the resistor's column is taken as the anode.

Each resistor straddles the centre gap, from row f of the upper half to row e of the lower half, in the same column as the LED anode. A blue jumper from the Uno pin lands in the lower half of that column.
Uno pins 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 feed LEDs 1 to 6 left to right, as in the circuit image.

Each LED cathode column has a short black jumper to the top negative rail, and a black jumper runs from Uno GND (next to pin 13) to that rail. The exact rail hole numbers (tn.1, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23, 26) are estimates read from the image; all holes in one rail are one strip, so the choice doesn't change the circuit.
The manual lists 220 ohm resistors. The code array order (2,7,4,6,5,3) only changes the lighting order, not the wiring.
The built-in LED on pin 13 is on the Uno board, so no external LED is added.
Breadboard rows: catalogue bank 't' is rows a-e and bank 'b' is rows f-j. In the image rows f-j are at the top and rows a-e at the bottom, so button and resistor positions follow that.
The bottom rail with the black line is treated as the negative rail (bn) and the red-line rail as the positive rail (bp). The red wire goes to bp and the black wire to bn.
Rail hole numbers (bp.2, bn.2, bp.4, bn.9) are estimated from the image. The rail numbering is approximate.
The button legs sit in columns 4 and 6. Column 6 is the input side (pin 2 wire and resistor). Column 4 is the 5V side (orange wire to the + rail).
The resistor's right lead is placed in column 9 so that it meets the short black ground wire there. The image is ambiguous about the exact column.
The black wire from the Uno goes to the second GND header pin, treated as GND.2.
The resistor is 10 kOhm, entered as value=10000.
The breadboard image's upper half is labelled rows f-j; following the catalogue, rows f-j are bank 'b' (e.g. 6b.g). The image's lower half (rows a-e) is unused.
Rail hole numbers (tp.2, tp.6, tn.4, tn.13, tn.26) are approximate; each rail is one strip so only the rail matters.

Circuit follows the image and schematic: 5V -> photoresistor -> node on A0 -> 10k -> GND; D9 -> LED anode (bent/longer leg, col 22), LED cathode -> 220 ohm -> GND. The 220 ohm resistor and LED are in series, as in the schematic (resistor order swapped relative to the schematic, which is electrically equivalent).
The manual text mentions 'Analog input 2' in the circuit caption but the images and text use A0, so A0 is used.
Both breadboard ground wires go to the top negative rail, which is linked to Arduino GND by wire2.

The breadboard image labels the upper half rows j-f and the lower half rows e-a. Holes are named by row letter, so f-j is bank 'b' and a-e is bank 't', as in the catalogue naming. This puts the image's upper half in bank 'b'.

The rail holes are numbered from the left in the image. The red 5V wire is at the first hole of the lower + rail (bp.1). The black GND wire is at the first hole of the lower - rail (bn.1). The orange wire is at the third hole (bp.3). The short black wire is at about the 7th hole of the - rail (bn.7). The rail numbering is approximate.
The button straddles the centre gap. Side 1 (column 4) is fed from the + rail by the orange wire. Side 2 (column 6) goes to pin 2 and to the 10k pull-down resistor.
The resistor runs from column 6 to column 9, row c. The short black wire takes column 9 to the - rail, which is GND.
The black GND wire goes to the second GND pin on the Uno power header (GND.2).
The pin 2 wire is the teal one, plugged into 6b.i in the same column as the button's side 2.
The code is not part of the graph.
Breadboard rows follow the catalogue: bank 'b' = rows f-j (upper half in the picture), bank 't' = rows a-e (lower half in the picture). Column/hole numbers are estimated from the picture.

Each pushbutton straddles the centre gap: side 1 (1.l/1.r) sits in the upper half (f row) and side 2 (2.l/2.r) in the lower half (e row). 5V reaches side 1 via a rail wire; the Arduino input wire, the 10k pulldown resistor sit on side 2 (same strip).
Pin mapping from the circuit/schematic: D6 = left-click button, D5 = right, D4 = left, D3 = down, D2 = up.
Top + rail is 'tp' (5V), bottom - rail is 'bn' (GND). Rail hole indexes are approximate; the resistors' lower leads go to the bottom ground rail.
The micro-USB cable to the computer is mentioned in the text but not drawn, so it is not included. 10k resistor is value=10000 (ohms).
Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue convention: the visual upper half (rows f-j) is bank 'b', so holes are written like '4b.g'.

Pin 9 -> orange wire -> column 4; 220 ohm resistor spans columns 4 and 6 in row h; LED anode (bent, longer leg) in column 6, cathode in column 8; black wire from column 8 to the Uno GND pin next to pin 13 (GND.1 assumed).
Resistor column positions were read from the image; the left end of the resistor aligns with the orange wire's column 4.
The Claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorization (via claude.ai connector settings) before they can be used; they are not needed for this graph.
Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue convention: bank 'b' is rows f-j. The picture's upper half (rows f-j) is therefore bank 'b'.
Resistor spans columns 3 and 6 in row h. The orange wire from pin 9 is in column 3 (row g), so it shares a strip with resistor leg 1.
LED anode (longer, bent leg) is in column 6, sharing a strip with resistor leg 2. The cathode (shorter leg) is in column 8, which the black wire in row h connects to GND.
The black wire runs to the GND pin next to pin 13 (GND.1), as shown in the image.
Resistor is 220 ohm per the manual text and schematic. The LED is red per the image.
The tutorial's software parts (Processing, Max/MSP) and the USB connection to the computer are not modelled. The Uno's USB cable is not part of the circuit in the manual.
The breadboard in the image is drawn with rows f-j in the upper half and a-e in the lower half, so I used the row letters to pick the bank: f-j is bank 'b' and a-e is bank 't'.

The pushbutton straddles the centre gap, with legs in columns 4 and 6. The catalogue says 1.l and 1.r are always joined, and 2.l and 2.r likewise. I treated the column-4 legs (4b.f and 4t.e) as side 1 and the column-6 legs (6b.f and 6t.e) as side 2. This matches the manual: 5V goes to one side, and pin 2 plus the pull-down go to the other side.
Pin 2 (teal wire) lands in column 6 at row i. The resistor's left lead is in column 6 at row c, on the same side of the button as pin 2, so it is the pull-down.

The orange wire runs from column 4 (row c) to the bottom plus rail and carries 5V to the button's other side. The 10k resistor goes from column 6 to column 9. The short black wire goes from column 9 (row b) to the bottom minus rail.
The hole numbers on the rails (bp.1, bp.3, bn.1, bn.7) are my estimate, counting rail holes from the left end of the board in groups of five.
The black wire from the Arduino ends on a GND pin in the power header. I used GND.2, the second of the two GND pins. The image shows the pin but the exact catalogue port is a guess.
The resistor value is given as 10000 ohms, from the manual's 10k ohm.

Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue convention: bank 'b' holds rows f-j. In the image this is the upper half, labelled j..f.
Orange wire ends at column 3, row g. The resistor spans column 3 to column 6 on row h, so the pin 9 signal reaches the resistor through the column 3 strip.

LED: the bent (longer) leg is in column 6 and is taken as the anode. The straight leg is in column 8 and is the cathode. The black wire ends at 8b.h in the cathode's strip, going to the GND pin next to pin 13.
The Uno GND pin used is the one beside pin 13, mapped to GND.1.
The 220 ohm value comes from the schematic and the hardware list.
No external LED: the tutorial uses the built-in LED on pin 13, so it is not a separate part.
Potentiometer legs are read from the image as columns 10, 11, 12 in the bottom half (row e): outer legs GND (col 10) and VCC (col 12), middle leg is the wiper (SIG, col 11).

In the image the yellow wire's breadboard end is drawn at the top of the pot (around column 11, upper half). The schematic shows the wiper going to A0, so I placed it in the wiper strip, 11b.d. This assumes the pot's wiper is the middle leg.
Black wire goes to the second GND header socket in the Uno power header (GND.2). Red wire goes to 5V.
The board is shown powered over USB, but no USB cable appears in the circuit image, so none is included.
Breadboard bank naming follows the catalogue (rows a-e = 't', f-j = 'b'); the image draws rows f-j on top and a-e on the bottom.

The potentiometer legs sit in row e of columns 11, 12 and 13 (GND, wiper, 5V). The pot's wiper has a pin on the top side that the yellow wire touches; I modelled the yellow wire as attached directly to the pot's SIG port, since the schematic shows A0 on the wiper.
Black wire goes to the second GND pin of the Uno power header (GND.2), as drawn.
The USB cable to the computer and the Processing/Max software are not modelled.

Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue (bank 't' = top half rows a-e, 'b' = bottom half rows f-j). The image labels the top half j-f and the bottom half e-a, so I mapped by physical position: top half rows j,i,f -> t.a, t.b, t.e; bottom half rows e,d -> b.f, b.g.

Each LED sits in the top half with anode in column 7/10/13/16/19/22 and cathode in the next column (8/11/14/17/20/23). I read the longer leg on the left as the anode, matching the schematic, where the resistor feeds the anode.

Each resistor straddles the centre gap in the same column as its LED's anode: leg 1 in the top half, leg 2 in the bottom half. A blue wire from Arduino pins 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 reaches the bottom half of that column.

Each LED cathode column has a short black jumper to the top ground rail (tn). Rail hole numbers are approximate, read from the picture. The long black wire runs from the Arduino GND next to AREF (GND.1) to the same rail (tn.1).
The schematic shows 220 ohm resistors; the bill of materials says the same.
The first circuit image is the authority on the connections; the schematic agrees (pins 2-7 -> resistor -> LED -> GND).
No external resistor: the internal pull-up on pin 2 (INPUT_PULLUP) is used; pin 13 uses the onboard LED, so no external LED is added.
Breadboard row naming: the image shows rows a-e on the lower half, which the catalogue calls bank 't' (rows a-e), so the lower-half holes are written as 10t/12t and the upper-half (f-j) as 10b/12b.

The pushbutton straddles the centre gap at columns 10 and 12. Legs in the same column are one side of the switch (side 1 = column 10, side 2 = column 12). Each of the four legs now has both a joined and an electrical edge to its breadboard hole, which fixes the 'leg not connected' warnings for sides 1 and 2.

Teal wire goes from Arduino pin 2 to column 10 (row c); black wire goes from the power-header GND (GND.1) to column 12 (row c). The image does not show which GND pin exactly; GND.1 on the power header is assumed.
The USB cable to the computer for serial is not drawn in the circuit image and is omitted.
Wiring follows the circuit image and schematic: 5V to VCC, A0 to VERT, A1 to HORZ, pin 6 to SEL (the joystick button), GND to GND.

The tutorial says the x-axis is on A0 and the y-axis on A1. The image labels the joystick pins VER/HOR and the schematic labels them VERT/HORZ. I used A0 to VERT and A1 to HORZ, as the schematic shows.

In the image the joystick's 5 header pins sit in one breadboard column. That would short them together, so I wired the jumpers straight to the joystick pins. The joystick only rests on the breadboard (contact edge, no hole-level joins).

The optional status LED on pin 5 is included: pin 5 to a 220 ohm resistor to the LED anode, and the LED cathode to GND. The tutorial gives no layout, so the breadboard holes are my own choice (20t, 24t, 25t). This LED circuit is not drawn in the manual's images.
The optional second pushbutton (D3 with a 10k pulldown) is only mentioned in text as optional, so I left it out.
The Leonardo's GND.1 (next to 5V on the power header) is used for the joystick, and GND.2 for the LED. The manual doesn't say which GND pin to use, so this is an assumption.
The USB cable to the computer is mentioned in the text but is not in the circuit image, so I didn't model it.
No external resistor: the sketch uses INPUT_PULLUP on pin 2, so pressing the button pulls pin 2 to GND.

The breadboard image labels the upper half rows f-j and the lower half rows a-e. The catalogue calls the a-e half bank 't' and the f-j half bank 'b', so the image's upper half is bank 'b' and its lower half is bank 't'.
The button straddles the centre gap with legs in columns 4 and 6. Side 1 is the upper pair (4b.f, 6b.f) and side 2 is the lower pair (4t.e, 6t.e).

The blue wire runs from Leonardo pin 2 to hole 6b.i, which is in the same strip as the button's upper legs. The black wire runs from the GND next to 5V (GND.1) to hole 4t.c, which is in the same strip as the button's lower-left leg.
The manual says the sketch also works on Micro or Due, but the diagram shows a Leonardo, so the Leonardo is used.

Breadboard coordinates read from the image: the button straddles the centre gap with legs in columns 4 and 6 (4t.e, 4b.f, 6t.e, 6b.f).

The blue wire goes from D2 to hole 6b.i, in the same strip as the button's column-6 legs. The black wire goes from the GND header next to 5V (GND.1) to 4t.c, in the same strip as the column-4 legs.
There is no external pull-up resistor. The sketch uses INPUT_PULLUP.
The diagram shows a Leonardo-style board, so arduino-leonardo is used. The GND pin labelled in the diagram is mapped to GND.1.
